ITEM
4. INFORMATION ON THE COMPANY
A.
History and Development of the Company.
Orangekloud
Technology Inc., the issuer in the IPO, was incorporated as an exempted company in the Cayman Islands on May 12, 2023.
Enterprise
Software Investment Inc. was incorporated on May 12, 2023 under the laws of the BVI as a holding company. Pursuant to the Reorganization
(as defined below), Enterprise Software Investment Inc. became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Orangekloud Technology Inc. on October 4,
2023.
MSC
Consulting (S) Pte. Ltd (“MSC Consulting”) was incorporated on June 16, 2003 as a private company limited by shares
under the laws of Singapore. MSC Consulting primarily engages in the operations of consulting, customizing, implementing, sales and after
sales support for Microsoft Dynamics Enterprise Resource Planning System.
Orangekloud
Pte. Ltd (“Orangekloud Singapore”) was incorporated on August 8, 2015 as a private company limited by shares under
the laws of Singapore. Orangekloud Singapore primarily engages in the operations of no-code platform and mobile application technology
and distributions.
Orangekloud
Investments Pte. Ltd (“Orangekloud Investments”, formerly known as Orangekloud Reskilling Centre Pte. Ltd) was incorporated
on November 8, 2018 as a private company limited by shares under the laws of Singapore. As at the date of this report, Orangekloud Investments
is an investment holding company currently holding a minority stake in a cybersecurity company in Singapore.
Orangekloud,
Inc. (“Orangekloud USA”) was incorporated on March 15, 2017, a California corporation. Orangekloud USA has been dormant
during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2025. Orangekloud USA is currently dormant as at the date of this report.
25
Orangekloud
Technology Sdn. Bhd. (“Orangekloud Malaysia”, formerly known as MSCI Consulting Sdn. Bhd.) was incorporated on May
16, 2006 as a private company limited by shares under the laws of Malaysia. Orangekloud Malaysia engages in the operations of support
arm for the Singapore business units.
On
July 24, 2024, the Company entered into an underwriting agreement with Maxim Group LLC as underwriter named thereof, in connection with
its initial public offering (“IPO”) of 2,750,000 Class A ordinary shares, par value $0.001 per share at a price of $4.75
per share. The Company’s Registration Statement on Form F-1 (File No. 333-277162) for the IPO, originally filed with the U.S. Securities
and Exchange Commission on February 20, 2024, as amended, was declared effective by the Commission on July 24, 2024. On July 30, 2024,
Maxim Group LLC notified the Company of their decision to further exercise the over-allotment option to purchase an additional 409,000
Class A ordinary shares of the Company, par value $0.001, at a price of $4.75 per share. The closing for the sale of the Over-allotment
Shares took place on August 1, 2024.
eMOBIQ AI Pte. Ltd (“eMOBIQ
AI”) was incorporated on July 24, 2025 as a private company limited by shares under the laws of Singapore. eMOBIQ AI was set
up with the intention of handling the licensing and subscription of the eMOBIQ AI platform and solutions at a later stage. As of the date
of this Report, eMOBIQ AI has not commenced business operations.
Reorganization
On
October 4, 2023, the Company consummated a reorganization (the “Reorganization”), pursuant to which the Company now
holds 100% of the shares in Enterprise Software Investment Inc, and Enterprise Software Investment Inc. now holds 100% of the shares
in MSC Consulting. The purpose of the Reorganization was to effect the Group’s internal restructuring for the Listing, following
which the shareholders of MSC Consulting became shareholders of the Company. MSC Consulting holds 100% of the shares in both Orangekloud
Singapore and Orangekloud Reskilling, while Orangekloud Singapore holds 100% of the shares in both Orangekloud, Inc. and MSCI Consulting.
The
Reorganization process was as follows:
On
September 5, 2023, Goh Jing Rui and Goh Jun Jia entered into an agreement with Enterprise Software Investment Inc., Goh Kian Hwa and
Lung Lay Hua, to each subscribe for 49 shares in Enterprise Software Investment Inc. for a consideration of $49.00 each, as well as a
condition subsequent for Goh Jing Rui and Goh Jun Jia, to make payment in aggregate, of S$125,000 to each of Goh Kian Hwa and Lung Lay
Hua, following their subscription of shares in Enterprise Software Investment Inc. for the consideration of which is the transfer of
their total shareholding in MSC Consulting Enterprise Software Investment Inc.
On
September 8, 2023, the shareholders of MSC Consulting, namely Goh Kian Hwa, Lung Lay Hua, and Chew Kim Chwee, subscribed for shares in
Enterprise Software Investment Inc., the consideration of which is the transfer of their total shareholding in MSC Consulting to Enterprise
Software Investment Inc. Following the subscription, Enterprise Software Investment Inc. held 100% shareholding of MSC Consulting. On
September 8, 2023, Chew Kim Chwee subscribed for 25 ordinary shares in Enterprise Software Investment Inc., the consideration of which
is the transfer of his 5,000 ordinary shares in MSC Consulting to Enterprise Software Investment Inc. On September 8, 2023, BDA Capital
Holding Inc, subscribed for 49 shares of Enterprise Software Investment Inc., for a consideration of US$49.00.
On
October 4, 2023, the shareholders of Enterprise Software Investment Inc., including Goh Kian Hwa, Lung Lay Hua, Goh Jing Rui, Goh Jun
Jia, Tan Kevin Patrick So, Chew Kim Chwee and BDA Capital Holding Inc, subscribed for shares in the Company, the consideration of which
is the transfer of their total shareholding in Enterprise Software Investment Inc. to the Company. The Company issued 499,012 Class A
Ordinary Shares to Chew Kim Chwee, in consideration for his 25 shares held in Enterprise Software Investment Inc. The Company issued
980,000 Class A Ordinary Shares to BDA Capital Holding Inc in consideration for the 49 shares held in Enterprise Software Investment
Inc.
Following
the consummation of the Reorganization, Goh Kian Hwa and Lung Lay Hua, who prior to the Reorganization held 48.43% and 48.95% respectively,
of the shares and voting powers of MSC Consulting, each held 7,485,494 Class B Ordinary Shares, representing 37.43% of the total Ordinary
Shares, or 48.38% of the voting power of the Company. Tan Kevin Patrick So, who prior to the Reorganization held 0% of MSC Consulting,
now holds 600,000 Class A Ordinary Shares representing 3% of the total Ordinary Shares, or 0.39% of the voting power of the Company.
26
Following
the Reorganization, Chew Kim Chwee held 499,012 Class A Ordinary Shares in the Company, or 2.50% shareholding of the Company. During
the past 3 years from the date of this report, Chew Kim Chwee was a shareholder and director of pre-sales of MSC Consulting.
Following
the Reorganization, BDA Capital Holding Inc, wholly owned by Goh Song Han, held 980,000 Class A Ordinary Shares in the Company, or 4.90%
shareholding of the Company.
These
transactions were not registered under the Securities Act in reliance on an exemption from registration set forth in Regulation S thereof.
IPO
On
July 24, 2024, the Company entered into an underwriting agreement with Maxim Group LLC as underwriter named thereof, in connection with
its initial public offering (“IPO”) of 2,750,000 Class A ordinary shares, par value US$0.001 per share at a price
of $4.75 per share. The Company’s Registration Statement on Form F-1 (File No. 333-277162) for the IPO, originally filed with the
U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on February 20, 2024, as amended, was declared effective by the Commission on July 24, 2024.
On July 30, 2024, Maxim Group LLC notified the Company of their decision to further exercise the over-allotment option to purchase an
additional 409,000 Class A ordinary shares of the Company, par value US$0.001 each, at a price of $4.75 per share. The closing for the
sale of the Over-allotment Shares took place on August 1, 2024.
Following
the consummation of the IPO, the exercise of over-allotment option by Maxim Group, Goh Kian Hwa and Lung Lay Hua, each held 7,485,494
Class B Ordinary Shares, representing 32.32% of the total Ordinary Shares, or 47.41% of the voting power of the Company. Tan Kevin Patrick
So, held 600,000 Class A Ordinary Shares representing 2.59% of the total Ordinary Shares, or 0.38% of the voting power of the Company.
BDA Capital Holding Inc, wholly owned by Goh Song Han, holds 980,000 Class A Ordinary Shares in the Company, or 4.23% shareholding of
the Company.
Share
Issuance after IPO
On
October 7, 2024, 200,000 Class A ordinary shares of the Company, par value US$0.001 each, were issued to Maxim Partners LLC as compensation
for the provision of general advisory and investment banking services to the Company.
Reverse
Stock Split
On
September 29, 2025, the Company’s 1-for-4 reverse stock split became effective. Following this, the Company’s total number
of Ordinary Shares outstanding became 5,839,770 (with the rounding up of some fractional shares following the reverse split),
comprising 2,087,022 Class A Ordinary Shares and 3,742,748 Class B Ordinary Shares. Goh Kian Hwa and Lung Lay Hua each held 1,871,374
Class B Ordinary Shares, representing 32.045% of the total Ordinary Shares and 49.72% of the voting power of the Company.
Tan Kevin Patrick So held 150,000 Class A Ordinary Shares, representing 2.57% of the total Ordinary Shares and 0.04% of the voting power
of the Company.
Capitalization
of Intercompany Debt
In
December 2025, MSC Consulting’s debt of S$5,300,000 (equivalent to US$4,061,000) owing to Orangekloud Technology Inc. (ORKT) was
novated to Enterprise Software Investment Inc. (ESI). Following the novation, ESI became the creditor of MSC Consulting for the S$5,300,000,
and ESI owed a corresponding amount of US$4,061,000 to ORKT. Subsequently, MSC Consulting issued 5,300,000 ordinary shares at S$1.00
each to ESI in full settlement of the debt. At the same time, ORKT subscribed for 20,305 ordinary shares of ESI for US$4,061,000, thereby
settling ESI’s obligation to ORKT. Upon completion of the capitalization exercise, ORKT continued to hold 100% of ESI, and ESI
continued to hold 100% of MSC Consulting. The share capital of ESI and MSC Consulting was strengthened by the above amounts, with no
change in consolidated ownership.
Share
Conversion
On
March 9, 2026, Goh Kian Hwa and Lung Lay Hua each converted 1,462,590 Class B Ordinary Shares to Class A Ordinary Shares. Following the
conversion, Goh Kian Hwa and Lung Lay Hua each held 408,784 Class B Ordinary Shares and 1,462,590 Class A Ordinary Shares, representing
32.045% of the total Ordinary Shares and 48.79% of the voting power of the Company.
Controlled
Company
As
of the date of this report, our directors, officers and principal shareholders hold in aggregate 66.66% or more of our Ordinary Shares
representing 97.75% of our total voting power in the aggregate. Although we will not be considered a “controlled company”
under Nasdaq corporate governance rules as we do not currently expect that more than 50% of our voting power will be held by an individual,
a group or another company immediately following the consummation of our IPO, the abovementioned shareholders, if they act together,
will be able to control the management and affairs of our Company.
B.
Business overview
We
are a holding company incorporated in the Cayman Islands with operations conducted by our Singapore and Malaysia subsidiaries, and are
headquartered in Singapore. Through our operating subsidiaries in predominantly Singapore, we position our Group as an AI-powered No-Code
software development platform provider specializing in hyper-automation solutions for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs).
As
a holding company incorporated in the Cayman Islands with no material operations, we conduct our operations in Singapore and Malaysia
through our operating subsidiaries: MSC Consulting primarily engages in the operations of consulting, customizing, implementing, sales
and after-sales support for Microsoft Dynamics Enterprise Resource Planning System. Orangekloud Singapore primarily engages in the operations
of no-code platform and mobile application technology and distributions, and has since 2024 invested significantly in the development
of Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities of its platform and solutions, culminating in a strategic enhancement in 2025 toward AI-driven
hyper-automation. Orangekloud Malaysia Consulting engages in the operations of support arm for Singapore business units. The Company
also has a holding company subsidiary, Enterprise Software Investment Inc., while the subsidiaries Orangekloud USA and Orangekloud Investments
(as defined hereunder in this report) are currently dormant and an investment holding company, respectively.
27
Our
digital transformation projects include the sales and consulting of Microsoft Dynamics ERP software licenses, as well as various steps
in the project implementation, including solution architecture consultancy, business process re-mapping, system customization and customer
support. We are also a certified Independent Software Vendor (“ISV”), providing our solutions for both Microsoft Dynamics
365 Business Central and Acumatica Cloud ERP.
In
2025, we undertook a strategic enhancement to position ourselves as a specialized provider of AI and Hyper-Automation solutions for SMEs.
We empower SMEs by integrating AI capabilities into their everyday business operations, driving efficiency, reducing manual tasks, and
enabling intelligent decision-making at scale. Building on our historical foundation as a No-Code platform provider, the Company now
focuses on delivering AI-driven digital transformation projects, including consulting and implementation for integration with Microsoft
Dynamics ERP software and our ISV solutions for Microsoft and Acumatica ERP. Through our AI-enhanced Rapid Mobile Application Development
(“RMAD”) platform, eMOBIQ®, and our web portal solution, OK365, the Company enables SMEs to develop intelligent enterprise
mobile and web applications, integrate ERP systems, and achieve end-to-end automation. These initiatives align with Singapore’s
“SME Go Digital”1 program and national AI innovation priorities, while strengthening the Company’s positioning
as an AI-first automation partner for SMEs.
Our
RMAD platform, eMOBIQ®, provides a No-Code development environment enhanced with AI Agent technology that focuses on enterprise mobile
and web application solutions with easy-to-use navigation tools, drag-and-drop application building components, and seamless integration
to various ERP systems and portals. The 2025 architectural upgrade allows applications built on eMOBIQ® to not merely display data but
actively “reason” and execute tasks through embedded AI capabilities. This significant enhancement allows us to rapidly develop
intelligent custom application solutions for customers, as well as enable customers who subscribe to our eMOBIQ® platform to build AI-powered
applications without requiring deep technical expertise in artificial intelligence or machine learning.
Specialized
AI Solutions for Vertical Industries
In
late 2025, the Company worked towards expanding its portfolio with specialized AI solutions designed to address industry-specific workflows
in high-volume transaction sectors. As of the date of this report, the Company has launched the AI WhatsApp Sales Ordering Solution for
food manufacturing and wholesale businesses, which leverages natural language processing to convert unstructured chat messages into structured
ERP-integrated sales orders, reducing errors and accelerating order cycles. The Company also deepened its integration within the Microsoft
ecosystem, deploying generative AI assistants through Microsoft Copilot and building hyper-automation flows with Power Platform and Power
Automate to streamline sales, finance, and operations. Enhanced by AI Agent capabilities within the eMOBIQ® platform, the Company enables
SMEs across industries such as food service, precision engineering, construction, retail, energy, and warehouse management to rapidly
develop intelligent mobile and web applications, optimize inventory through predictive analytics, and deliver personalized customer experiences
at scale.
Singapore
Government Support for AI Innovation and Adoption
The
Singapore government has made AI and automation strategic national priorities, creating a comprehensive support framework that directly
benefits the Company and its SME customers. Under the National AI Strategy 2.0, expanded in 2025, initiatives such as AI Singapore provide
research funding, talent development, and industry partnerships, which have accelerated the development of AI Agent capabilities in our
eMOBIQ® platform. SMEs adopting our solutions also benefit from grants and tax incentives, including the Enterprise Development Grant,
Productivity Solutions Grant, and enhanced R&D and innovation deductions, as well as new SME tax savings on AI solutions announced
in Budget 2026. In addition, the Infocomm Media Development Authority’s SME Go Digital program prioritizes AI adoption through
sector-specific Industry Digital Plans, Start Digital initiatives, and Advanced Digital Solutions funding. Collectively, these measures
significantly reduce the cost of AI adoption, strengthen ROI for SMEs, and align our offerings with Singapore’s national strategy
to drive productivity and competitiveness through widespread AI deployment.
Gen
AI and Digital Leaders Program
As
of the date of this report, MSC Consulting has been approved by the Singapore Infocomm Media Development Authority (“IMDA”)
as a Gen AI x Digital Leaders provider under the SMEs Go Digital Program, representing formal government recognition of our capabilities
in delivering AI-powered digital transformation solutions to Singapore’s SME sector. Through this designation, our eMOBIQ AI-enhanced
platform and AI WhatsApp Sales Ordering Solution are pre-qualified for grant funding support, enabling SMEs to adopt our solutions with
expedited approval processes and enhanced financial incentives. The Digital Leaders recognition further endorses our ability to deliver
AI automation solutions, while IMDA’s network assists to refer SMEs to approved providers, creating a government-facilitated pipeline
that complements our direct sales efforts. This partnership aligns with our strategic enhancement toward AI-driven automation and provides
both validation of our capability and commercial advantages through funding access and customer referrals.

28
Industry
overview
Digital
Transformation and AI Adoption. SME digital transformation in Singapore has evolved from basic digitization to intelligent automation.
Surveys by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) show that recommended digital solutions have delivered significant efficiency
gains, with 85% of SMEs reporting time savings and 75% noting reduced reliance on manual labor. By 2025, market expectations shifted
decisively toward AI-first solutions, driven by labor market pressures, national productivity targets, competitive dynamics, and the
maturity of technologies such as large language models and generative AI. Updated Industry Digital Plans now emphasize AI and automation
as priority technologies, supported by government grants such as the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) and Productivity Solutions Grant
(PSG). 3
Challenges
for AI Transformation. Despite clear imperatives, SMEs face barriers including complexity in technology selection, limited implementation
resources and know-how, uncertain ROI, and fragmented data readiness. These challenges make AI adoption difficult without accessible
platforms and government support.
Challenges
for Traditional Digital Transformation. SMEs also continue to struggle with packaged software limitations and the drawbacks of
customized solutions, which often result in high costs, long deployment timelines, ongoing maintenance burdens, and siloed systems. Scarcity
of developer resources further compounds these issues.
Low-Code/No-Code
Market Opportunity. Low-Code/No-Code platforms have emerged as a solution, enabling faster, simpler, and more cost-effective
application development. Market research projects strong growth, with Gartner forecasting that 70% of new enterprise applications will
be built using low-code/no-code technologies by 2025. Microsoft anticipates that 90% of the 500 million apps created over the next five
years will be designed on such platforms.
AI
Integration with Low-Code/No-Code. By 2025, leading platforms have evolved into AI-enhanced environments, incorporating AI Agents,
natural language interfaces, and intelligent automation. This convergence addresses both application development and AI implementation
challenges, accelerating SME adoption of sophisticated AI solutions without requiring specialized expertise.
Geographic
Market Dynamics. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing low-code/no-code market, driven by government digitalization
initiatives, smartphone penetration, and IT sector expansion. Singapore’s position as a regional technology hub, combined with
strong government incentives and IMDA partnership frameworks, creates favorable conditions for rapid AI automation adoption among SMEs.

According
to Prescient & Strategic Intelligence Private Limited (“Prescient & Strategic”), the global Low-Code development
platform market revenue was approximately $12,500.6 million in 2020, and is predicted to witness an approximate 31.3% CAGR between 2020
to 2030, to reach approximately $190,792.6 million by 2030.4 .Moreover, according to the latest forecast from Gartner, Inc.,
the worldwide market for Low-Code development technologies is projected to total approximately $26.9 billion in 2023, an increase of
19.6% from 2022.5 Low-Code application platforms are projected to be the largest component of the Low-Code development technology
market which includes but not limited to business process automation, multi-experience development platforms, robotic process automation,
etc., growing approximately 25% to reach nearly $10 billion in 2023. Microsoft anticipates that the 500 million apps it expects will
be created over the next five years, 450 million will be designed on No-Code/Low-Code platforms.6 According to Gartner, Inc.,
a key factor to drive the Low-Code development technologies through 2026 is the rise in business technologists and a growing number of
enterprise-wide hyper automation and composable business initiatives will be the key drivers accelerating the adoption of Low-Code technologies
through 2026. Further, another key factor was the COVID-19 pandemic, which drove a significant increase in the demand for computer and
mobile applications offering news and gaming, COVID-19 related alerts, and other features, during general lockdowns and movement restrictions.
According to Prescient & Strategic, in the years to come, Asia-Pacific (“APAC”) will be the fastest-growing Low-Code
development platform market on account of the increasing focus of governments on digital transformation, burgeoning smartphone and internet
penetration, and expanding IT sector. Moreover, a lot of North American and European companies outsource application and software development
to those based in APAC, which is driving the usage of this technology.
Our
opportunities
We
believe we have a significant market opportunity in helping organizations streamline their operations and achieve intelligent automation
by leveraging on our AI-enhanced No-Code eMOBIQ® platform:
●
AI-First
Market Positioning. The 2025 market landscape presents a significant opportunity
for platforms that bridge the AI implementation gap for SMEs. While large enterprises can
deploy custom AI solutions, SMEs require accessible, pre-configured capabilities. Our eMOBIQ®
platform, with integrated AI Agents, delivers enterprise-grade automation without specialized
expertise.
Constraints
of Traditional Application Development Models. Traditional mobile application development is costly, time-consuming, and
dependent on scarce developer resources. In contrast, our AI-enhanced RMAD platform empowers both professional and citizen developers
to build sophisticated applications quickly and cost-effectively, reducing reliance on external developers and lowering total cost
of ownership.
Market
Demand for AI-Enhanced Low-Code/No-Code Technologies. Global demand for low-code/no-code platforms is expanding rapidly,
with forecasts projecting strong growth through 2030. Gartner reports that a majority of custom applications are now built outside
IT departments, often by non-technical users. By embedding AI capabilities, our platform enables business leaders to create intelligent
applications, broadening our addressable market beyond traditional IT buyers.
Government
Support Acceleration. Singapore’s comprehensive support framework—including grants, SME tax savings on AI solutions,
IMDA Digital Leaders approval, and government referrals—reduces adoption barriers and strengthens ROI for SMEs. These measures
de-risk customer investment decisions and provide predictable growth conditions for our platform.
●
WhatsApp
Commerce Opportunity. The launch of our AI WhatsApp Sales Ordering Solution validates a major opportunity in conversational
commerce. With WhatsApp’s global penetration, particularly in APAC, our solution formalizes existing B2B ordering behavior
in food distribution and extends to other high-volume transaction industries such as pharmaceuticals, building materials, and consumer
goods
●
End-to-end
solution. Our eMOBIQ® platform supports integration from front-end processing to back-end systems, enabling enterprise
solutions such as field service applications. AI enhancements allow autonomous decision-making in areas like routing, predictive
maintenance, and resource allocation, further strengthening customer digital transformation outcomes.
●
Microsoft
& Acumatica Partner Network Leverage. Strong partnerships with Microsoft and Acumatica, combined with seamless integration
connectors, allow us to tap into their extensive partner and customer ecosystems. As these vendors expand AI capabilities within
their platforms, our AI-enhanced eMOBIQ® solution complements and extends their offerings to mobile and custom application scenarios.

Our
competitive strengths
We
believe our main competitive strengths are as follows:
●
AI-Enhanced
No-Code Platform. Our in-house RMAD platform, eMOBIQ®, provides an AI-enhanced No-Code environment for enterprise mobile
and web applications. The 2025 upgrade introduced autonomous AI Agents capable of reasoning, predictive analytics, and automated
decision-making, enabling SMEs to deploy intelligent automation without data science teams. With drag-and-drop tools and intuitive
interfaces, both professional and citizen developers can rapidly build custom applications that streamline operations at lower cost.
Microsoft
Ecosystem Deep Integration. As a Microsoft Gold Partner with ISV certification for Dynamics 365 Business Central, we deliver
deep integration that competitors cannot easily replicate. Pre-built connectors, Copilot deployment expertise, and Power Platform
automation flows allow SMEs to maximize existing Microsoft investments while achieving hyper-automation across sales, finance, and
operations.
Cross
Mobile Platform Compatibility. Applications built on eMOBIQ® can be deployed across iOS, Android, and web platforms from
a single codebase, with access to native device functionalities such as camera, NFC, and GPS. This broad compatibility ensures flexibility
and scalability for customers across diverse environments.
●
Comprehensive
AI-Driven Digital Transformation Solutions. We provide end-to-end digital transformation solutions by combining ERP implementations
with AI-enhanced enterprise mobile applications developed on eMOBIQ®. These tailored solutions embed intelligent automation that
continuously optimizes business processes and operational efficiency.
●
Government-Validated
Solution Provider. Our approval as an IMDA Gen AI and Digital Leaders vendor under the SMEs Go Digital Program provides strong
competitive differentiation. Government endorsement reduces customer risk perception, pre-qualified grant status accelerates adoption,
and IMDA referrals generate qualified leads, advantages that are difficult for competitors to replicate.
●
Integration
with major ERP Vendor with eMOBIQ® Connector. eMOBIQ® offers ready-built connectors to Microsoft Dynamics, Acumatica,
and SAP Business One, enabling seamless integration with critical business data and reducing the need for custom development.
●
Experienced
management team. Our management team combines deep industry domain knowledge with AI expertise developed through partnerships
with AI Singapore and internal capability building. This ensures we can guide SMEs through both digital transformation and AI adoption
journeys with comprehensive support.
Our
business strategies
Our
business strategies and future plans are as follows:
●
Continue
to Innovate with Focus on AI-Enhanced eMOBIQ Platform. We will continue investing in research and development to strengthen
our eMOBIQ® platform and expand AI-driven features. The 2025 integration of AI Agents marked a major milestone, with future priorities
including advanced multi-step workflow automation, generative AI for application creation, predictive analytics modules, and expanded
conversational AI capabilities. Ongoing upgrades and collaborations with partners on emerging technologies such as large language
models, voice-directed development, and blockchain will further enhance platform functionality and adoption.
●
Marketing
Campaign Focused on AI Value Proposition. We plan to grow eMOBIQ® license revenues through targeted campaigns emphasizing
our AI-first positioning and measurable ROI. Marketing will highlight productivity gains, government tax savings and grant support,
IMDA endorsement, and real-world case studies. With SMEs expected to grow software adoption at a CAGR of 24% through 2030, we see
significant opportunity to expand our customer base across industries including food manufacturing, logistics, retail, construction,
energy, and warehouse management.9

●
Expand
Digital Transformation Business Beyond Singapore and Malaysia. Over time, we intend to expand globally through direct sales,
channel partnerships, and potential mergers and acquisitions, leveraging Microsoft Dynamics, Acumatica, and Zebra Technologies partner
networks. Geographic priorities include Hong Kong, Australia, UAE, and select European markets with strong SME sectors, high labor
costs, and government digital transformation incentives. We also intend to broaden ISV offerings to ERPs such as Sage, SAP Business
One HANA, and Epicor.
●
Grow
revenue from key industry verticals. We will continue enhancing vertical solutions through eMOBIQ®, focusing on food
manufacturing and distribution, logistics and warehouse management, retail, and construction. Planned AI solutions include demand
forecasting, production scheduling, route optimization, predictive maintenance, intelligent inventory management, and project scheduling
automation.
●
Growing
market presence through universities, software development houses and community. We are working with universities in Malaysia
and Indonesia to expand adoption of eMOBIQ among students, creating a pipeline of platform-experienced developers. Community versions
of the platform will further build awareness and advocacy. Partnerships with software development houses and consulting firms will
extend customer coverage and solution delivery capabilities.
●
Expand
strategic partnerships. We aim to broaden our partner base across Microsoft partners, system integrators, industry-specific
vendors, and consulting firms. These partnerships will accelerate project delivery, add mobile and AI capabilities to existing practices,
and generate referrals from organizations advising SMEs on digital transformation strategies.
Our
products and services
At
present, we provide consultation and implementation of AI-enabled digital transformation solutions to SMEs and large enterprises with
a focus on the Singapore market.
Packaged
Software Solutions
We
offer digital transformation solutions to SMEs in Singapore through implementations of Enterprise Resource Planning (“ERP”)
systems coupled with our AI-enhanced Enterprise Mobile Application solutions developed using our eMOBIQ® platform. Our SME customers traditionally
become aware of our products and services through seminars or webinars to potential customers, as well as through referrals by existing
or previous customers, and increasingly through IMDA advisor referrals. Our sales and marketing team also performs telemarketing to target
customers focused on specific industries.
Our
digital transformation projects include sales and consulting of Microsoft Dynamics ERP software licenses, as well as various steps in
project implementation, including solution architecture consultancy, business process re-mapping, system customization and customer support,
now enhanced with AI-powered automation capabilities.
32
Solution
Architecture Consultancy
According
to a 2021 SME survey by Infocomm Media Development Authority, digital solutions recommended by Industry Digital Plans (“IDP”)
brought about improvement in overall efficiency in work processes, with around 85 percent of respondents observing time savings and 75
percent sharing that manpower-efficient digital solutions enabled them to be less dependent on manual labour.
By
2025, our consultancy approach has evolved to incorporate AI readiness assessment and intelligent automation roadmapping. Our information
technology team provides on-site consultancy for customers, reviewing business needs and existing infrastructure and providing guidance
on possible solutions that leverage AI capabilities to achieve maximum productivity gains. After initial consultation, our sales team
provides quotations on suggested solution packages based on initial review, including projected ROI from AI automation components.
Business
Process Remapping
The
final design is presented to customers. Upon customers deciding on suggested solution approaches and agreeing to quotations, our information
technology team implements remapping of business processes, installing packaged ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central
enhanced with AI-powered automation workflows. These systems provide digital backbones to Customers’ new ERP systems while embedded
AI capabilities continuously optimize processes based on actual usage patterns.

Our

Workplace
Safety and Health Act
The
Workplace Safety and Health Act 2006 of Singapore (the “WSHA”) is the principal legislation governing the safety, health
and welfare of persons at work in workplaces. Among other things, the WSHA imposes a duty on every employer and every principal (which
would include us) to take, so far as is reasonably practicable, such measures as are necessary to ensure the safety and health of its
employees, and any contractor, any direct or indirect subcontractor, and any employee employed by such contractor or subcontractor, when
at work.
The
general penalties for non-compliance with the WSHA include the imposition of fines up to the amount of S$500,000 in the case of a body
corporate. Further or other penalties may apply in the case of repeat offences or specific offences under the WSHA or its subsidiary
legislation.
Employment
Act
The
Employment Act 1968 of Singapore, or the Singapore EA, sets out the basic terms and conditions of employment and the rights and responsibilities
of employers as well as employees. With effect from 1 April 2019, the Singapore EA extends to all employees, including persons employed
in managerial or executive positions, with certain exceptions.
The
Singapore EA prescribes certain minimum conditions of service that employers are required to provide to their employees, including (i)
minimum days of statutory annual and sick leave; (ii) paid public holidays; (iii) statutory protection against wrongful dismissal; (iv)
provision of key employment terms in writing; and (v) statutory maternity leave and childcare leave benefits. In addition, certain statutory
protections relating to overtime and hours of work are prescribed under the Singapore EA, but only apply to limited categories of employees,
such as an employee (other than a workman) who is not employed in a managerial or executive position and who receives a salary of up
to S$2,600 a month (“relevant employee”). Section 38(8) of the Singapore EA provides that a relevant employee is not allowed
to work for more than 12 hours in any one day except in specified circumstances, such as where the work is essential to the life of the
community, defense or security. In addition, section 38(5) of the Singapore EA limits the extent of overtime work that a relevant employee
can perform, to 72 hours a month.
43
Other
employment-related benefits which are prescribed by law include (i) contributions to be made by an employer to the Central Provident
Fund, under the Central Provident Fund Act 1953 of Singapore in respect of each employee who is a citizen or permanent resident of Singapore;
(ii) the provision of statutory maternity, paternity, childcare, adoption, unpaid infant care and shared parental leave benefits (in
each case subject to the fulfilment of certain eligibility criteria) under the Child Development Co-savings Act 2001 of Singapore; (iii)
statutory protections against dismissal on the grounds of age, and statutory requirements to offer re-employment to an employee who attains
the prescribed minimum retirement age, under the Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993 of Singapore; and (iv) statutory requirements
relating to work injury compensation, and workplace safety and health, under the Work Injury Compensation Act 2019 of Singapore and the
Workplace Safety and Health Act 2006 of Singapore, respectively.
Central
Provident Fund Act
The
Central Provident Fund (“CPF”) system is a mandatory social security savings scheme funded by contributions from employers
and employees. Pursuant to the Central Provident Fund Act 1953 of Singapore (“CPFA”), an employer is obliged to make CPF
contributions for all employees who are Singapore citizens or permanent residents who are employed in Singapore by an employer (save
for employees who are employed as a master, a seaman or an apprentice in any vessel, subject to an exception for non-exempted owners).
CPF contributions are not applicable for foreigners who hold employment passes, S passes or work permits. CPF contributions are required
for both ordinary wages and additional wages (subject to an ordinary wage ceiling and a yearly additional wage ceiling) of employees
at the applicable prescribed rates which is dependent on, among other things, the amount of monthly wages and the age of the employee.
An employer must pay both the employer’s and employee’s share of the monthly CPF contribution. However, an employer can recover
the employee’s share of CPF contributions by deducting it from their wages when the contributions are paid for that month.
Where
the amount of the contributions which an employer is liable to pay under the CPFA in respect of any month is not paid within such period
as may be prescribed, the employer shall be liable for the payment of interest on the amount for every day the amount remains unpaid
commencing from the first day of the month succeeding the month in respect of which the amount is payable and the interest shall be calculated
at the rate of 1.5% per month or the sum of S$5, whichever is greater. Where any employer who has recovered any amount from the monthly
wages of an employee in accordance with the CPFA fails to pay the contributions to the CPF within such time as may be prescribed, he
will be guilty of an offense and will be liable on conviction for a fine not exceeding S$10,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding
seven years or both. Where an offense has been committed under the CPFA but there are no penalties provided, the offender may be liable
for a fine not exceeding S$5,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or both, and where the offense is repeated by the
same offender, the offender may be liable for a fine not exceeding S$10,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or both.
Personal
Data Protection Act 2012
The
Personal Data Protection Act 2012 of Singapore (“PDPA”) governs the collection, use and disclosure of the personal
data of individuals by organizations, and is administered and enforced by the regulator, the Personal Data Protection Commission. The
PDPA sets out data protection obligations which all organizations are required to comply with in undertaking activities relating to the
collection, use or disclosure of personal data. A failure to comply with any of the above can subject an organization to a fine of up
to the higher of S$1,000,000 or 10% of the organization’s annual turnover in Singapore (for an organization whose annual turnover
in Singapore exceeds S$10,000,000).
In
the course of operating their businesses, the Company’s subsidiaries collect and use personal data from consenting customers. The
Company’s subsidiaries have implemented various processes to safeguard the personal data collected from its customers, which include
the appointment of a Data Protection Officer with an appropriate level of knowledge and specific responsibilities to ensure data protection
within the Group, as well as providing data protection training to all employees of the Company’s subsidiaries.
The
Company’s subsidiaries believe that they are in compliance with all PDPA requirements. In addition, IFSC is undergoing an ISO 27001
certification project, which will demonstrate the company’s ability to meet the minimum threshold expected to protect personal
data. IFSC is also ISO 9001 certified, which shows that the internal processes to ensure data security are in place.
44
Regulations
on Anti-Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Financing
The
primary anti-money laundering legislation in Singapore is the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of
Benefits) Act 1992 of Singapore, or CDSA, provides for the confiscation of benefits derived from, and to combat, corruption, drug dealing
and other serious crimes. Generally, the CDSA criminalizes the concealment or transfer of the benefits of criminal conduct as well as
the knowing assistance of the concealment, transfer or retention of such benefits.
The
Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act 2002 of Singapore, or TSOFA, is the primary legislation for the combating of terrorism financing.
It was enacted to give effect to the International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism. Besides criminalizing
